entities.summary:
Nikolaus Decius (also Degius, Deeg, Tech a Curia, and Nickel von Hof; c. 1485 – 21 March 1541 was a German monk, hymn-writer, Protestant reformer and composer.

As a prominent figure in the early Protestant Reformation, Decius played a crucial role in shaping the theological and musical landscape of 16th-century Germany. Born in a small town in the Rhineland, Decius studied at the University of Cologne and later became a monk in the Benedictine Order. He composed numerous hymns, many of which were later incorporated into the Lutheran hymnal, and was a key figure in the development of Protestant liturgy.

Decius's most notable work is his collection of hymns, 'Tech a Curia,' which was first published in 1536 and went on to become a standard reference for Protestant hymns. His compositions, characterized by their beauty and theological depth, continue to be sung in churches and homes around the world.

Despite his significant contributions to the Protestant Reformation, Decius's life was marked by controversy and persecution. He faced opposition from Catholic authorities and was eventually forced to flee his homeland. Nevertheless, his legacy as a composer, reformer, and theologian remains an important part of Protestant heritage.

One of the most striking aspects of Decius's legacy is the enduring impact of his hymns on Christian worship. His compositions have been translated into numerous languages and continue to be sung in churches around the world. The legacy of 'Tech a Curia' is a testament to Decius's skill as a hymn-writer and his commitment to the Protestant cause.

In conclusion, Nikolaus Decius was a pivotal figure in the early Protestant Reformation, making significant contributions to the development of Protestant liturgy and hymns. His legacy continues to be felt in Christian worship around the world.
